evidence.text: The CUHK account interprets the oracle form of 老 as 人, 毛 and 丨, with 丨 representing a staff; the graph depicts a bent, long-haired person holding it, glossed as an elderly person. It reports bronze forms with the staff written 匕 and sometimes miswritten 止; later upper-part variants include one with 由, tentatively analyzed as phonetic. The 由 proposal concerns a later variant, not the original graph.
evidence.title: 漢語甲骨部件分析: 老

evidence.text: The entry reports an oracle-bone place-name occurrence, 合集22246, without an absolute date for that item. Its bronze examples include an elder, the adjective ‘old’ (五年召白虎𣪕, ‘余老’), senior ministers, and 老 used for 考 ‘father’. Warring States bamboo-text examples include 舜乃老 and 老夫. These are distinct reported uses; the entry does not establish a chronological chain connecting them.
evidence.title: 漢語甲骨部件分析: 老

evidence.source: ShuoWen.org, 說文解字 and 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The received Shuowen text (Eastern Han dictionary) glosses 老 as 考, says a person aged seventy is called 老, and analyzes the form as 人、毛、匕, explaining it through whitening hair. Qing commentator Duan Yucai records the reciprocal-gloss/轉注 discussion and proposes that the seal form may derive from 毛匕, with 人 not a separate element. These are later lexicographic analyses, not direct confirmation of the oracle graph’s origin.
evidence.title: 說文解字「老」

evidence.source: Chinese Text Project, 說文解字 老部
evidence.text: The displayed received Shuowen text gives 考也。七十曰老。从人、毛、匕 and also lists 考 as 从老省、丂聲 and 孝 as 从老省、从子. This attests Shuowen’s own analyses, not the ancient sound or graphic origin of 老.
evidence.title: 說文解字: 卷九: 老部

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry gives Mandarin lǎo and lists senses including elderly person, old in age, respectful address, respect elders, old/long-standing, obsolete, original, retired, experienced, frequent/intensifying uses, and prefix uses. Its quotations include Warring States citations such as Zhanguo Ce and Mencius, along with later works. A dictionary’s grouped quotations do not establish a complete chronology for these extensions.
evidence.title: A03251 老 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: The table gives 考 kǎo, Middle Chinese khawX, Old Chinese *k-r̥ˤuʔ, gloss ‘old; deceased father’, and 老 lǎo, Middle Chinese lawX, Old Chinese *C.rˤuʔ, gloss ‘old’. Its own distinct transcriptions must be preserved; comparison alone does not prove the proposed cognacy or a phonetic component in 老.

gaps: The earliest cited oracle instance is a place-name occurrence, but its relationship to 老’s lexical ‘old’ sense is not established; CUHK supplied no absolute date for that particular inscription.

The CUHK entry reports bronze and Warring States examples, but the artifacts or editions cited there were not inspected individually. Those reports do not prove a semantic chronology or explain the relationship between ‘old’ and 老 written for 考 ‘father’.

Graphic history is partially documented: the staff is described as 丨 in oracle forms, 匕 in bronze forms, and sometimes miswritten 止; later upper forms vary, with 由 only tentatively assigned a phonetic role in one later variant. The full sequence and causes are not established by inspected evidence.

The original SVG for 老-seal.svg could not be fetched, so no pixel-level identity inspection was possible. The other two supplied Commons file leads did not yield verified metadata. The local Commons manifest cannot by itself establish their current provenance or licensing.
Official Unihan pages for 老, 考, and 孝 could not be opened. Exact local kMandarin rows are recorded as local evidence and are not represented as upstream verification.

No local Baxter–Sagart or Unihan extract is recommended: the primary B–S PDF supports repeatable verification for 老 and 考, while the exact Unihan pages failed and no bulk reuse terms were verified for repeated dictionary sources.

No sound component is established for 老’s original graph. 孝’s resemblance and readings, and 老/考 reconstruction comparison, do not establish a phonetic role within 老. ShuoWen’s 老/考 reciprocal gloss and 轉注 discussion are historical analyses, not a demonstrated semantic history.
